(1) distributionally robust optimization over Wasserstein balls admits tractable reformulations in many interesting cases; (2) these reformulations admit performance guarantees in terms of the Wasserstein metric; and (3) these performance guarantees are sharp, i.e. the worst case distributional risk is attained at the boundary of the Wasserstein ball.

(1) the Wasserstein metric allows to construct a distributionally robust optimization problem whose solutions enjoy strong finite sample performance guarantees, and (2) the resulting distributionally-robust problems can be reformulated as tractable linear optimization problems in many interesting cases.
